children: The U.S. government on Monday moved to prevent the Singaporean company Megaspeed and its affiliates from buying American AI chips after pressure over the firm's alleged role in helping Nvidia funnel the advanced semiconductors to China.
The U.S. Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its Entity List, which prevents U.S. firms from doing business with listed companies unless they obtain a special license.

Megaspeed is under investigation by the Justice Department for allegedly helping Nvidia skirt U.S. export laws and sell chips into the Chinese market. Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who U.S. officials suspect of being a Chinese intelligence agent, also had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during the alleged chip smuggling. The Nvidia CEO previously resigned his post amid the scandal, but was reinstated on Monday.

The Commerce Department has been under pressure by other Trump administration officials to investigate Megaspeed, Nvidia and other entities involved in chip smuggling. In recent days, the administration has given national security adviser Marco Rubio more authority over the export control process for chips and other technologies, which is typically led by Commerce, The Wall Street Journal previously reported.
